boundary.role: the trigger: return smc.aux.ESS < smc.N * smc.ESSrmin
ESSrmin default 0.5; resampling scheme name default 'systematic'; N default 100
rs_flag = fk.time_to_resample(self); if set, A = rs.resampling(scheme, aux.W, M=N), Xp = X[A], weights reset; else A = identity; then X = M(t, Xp)
loglt = log mean weight if rs_flag or t == 0 else the difference of consecutive log mean weights; logLt accumulates
ESS = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 from log-weights, max-subtracted
the three classical schemes as ordered-uniform draws over one inverse-CDF pass (inverse_cdf at 485-510)

mechanism_claim.functional_claim: Within the SMC loop, whether the particle population is resampled at step t is decided by exactly one predicate -- ESS(aux weights) < N * ESSrmin, evaluated at core.py:181-183 and consumed at core.py:326-338 -- and resampling is the only operation that counteracts weight degeneracy. Consequently: (a) with ESSrmin = 0 the loop never resamples and the log-likelihood estimate logLt and the filtering means degrade with T; (b) with ESSrmin = 1 the loop resamples at every step t >= 1 whose weights are non-uniform; (c) with the trigger fixed, the variance of logLt is ordered by scheme, multinomial above systematic.
mechanism_claim.claimed_inputs: log-weights (from logG), N, ESSrmin, the scheme name
mechanism_claim.claimed_outputs: rs_flag per step; the ancestor vector A; the reset of the weights; through them logLt and the particle approximation of the filtering distribution
mechanism_claim.claimed_internal_dependency: time_to_resample reads aux.ESS (essl over the current log-weights, or the APF-adjusted ones); resample_move reads rs_flag and the scheme registry; compute_summaries reads rs_flag to choose the loglt form; no other CODE line in core.py reads ESS or ESSrmin (grep 2026-09-17 on payload 1c99eb98...: code sites 183, 264, 274; 212-217 are docstring)
mechanism_claim.known_uncertainty: the SIZE of the multinomial-vs-systematic variance gap at N = 100, T = 100 on the chosen model (theory orders them; the packet's band is wide); whether numba's JIT of inverse_cdf/ssp is available on the adjudicating host (it is on M3 as of the SCOUT import); the model-level default ESSrmin lives in SMC.__init__, not in the model class -- the cut's residue said 'not read', this packet corrects that: it is 0.5 at core.py:264

interventions.intervention_operation: no code change; SMC(fk, N=100, resampling='systematic', ESSrmin=0.5)
interventions.units: |B| in nats of log-likelihood (bias of the estimator across 50 seeds)
interventions.band_basis: the SMC likelihood estimator is unbiased in expectation (Del Moral); with N=100, T=100 and sigmaY=0.2 the log of an unbiased estimator has a negative bias of order V/2; V for this model at N=100 is expected in [0.05, 2] nats^2, so |B| <= 2 is a generous band, not a tight prediction

interventions.prediction_rationale: establishes V0, RMSE0, R0 against which I1-I3 are read; R0 is expected in [10, 90] of 99 eligible steps (sigmaY = 0.2 is informative, so degeneracy is frequent but not total)

interventions.units: V(I1)/V(I0), ratio of seed variances of logLt
interventions.band_basis: without resampling the weights degenerate to one particle within tens of steps at sigmaY=0.2; the estimator's variance grows roughly exponentially in T (Chopin & Papaspiliopoulos 2020, ch. 10); a factor of at least 5 at T=100 is conservative; the upper bound is a numerical cap

interventions.intervention_operation: SMC(fk, N=100, resampling='systematic', ESSrmin=1.0) -- the predicate ESS < N is true whenever the weights are not exactly uniform
interventions.band_basis: resampling at every step adds resampling noise on the steps where ESS was still high and removes none of the degeneracy that I0 already removes; the literature reports either a small increase or no change for systematic resampling; the band admits both signs

interventions.intervention_operation: SMC(fk, N=100, resampling='multinomial', ESSrmin=0.5) against I0
interventions.units: ratio of seed variances of logLt
interventions.band_basis: systematic resampling has lower conditional variance of the offspring counts than multinomial (Douc, Cappe & Moulines 2005); the effect on the likelihood estimator's variance at N=100 is expected small but positive; the lower edge 1.05 is the smallest ratio the 50-seed design can distinguish from 1 at roughly 2 standard errors (var of a variance ratio with 49 df each is ~ 4/49 => se ~ 0.29 -- so 1.05 is NOT distinguishable; see indeterminate: this row is underpowered by design and is the row most likely to return PREDICTION_INDETERMINATE; Harmonia may raise seeds to 400 to power it)
interventions.pressure_scope: the resampling-variance pressure stated in the cut
interventions.prediction_rationale: the scheme is the only difference between the arms; a ratio below 1/1.05 with adequate power would falsify the ordering claim (c) but NOT the boundary (a scheme ordering is a claim about the schemes, not about where the trigger lives): that outcome is PREDICTION_FAILED on (c), not CUT_KILL
